label: F-04
title: An untagged commit rewrites the annihilation settlement post-condition on top of a two-story fix-wave: no story authorises it, story-001 explicitly forbade touching that logic, and story-001's acceptance checklist still self-certifies that it was preserved
fingerprintNote: sha256(contract:function:rootCauseClass)[:16] - legacy form, empty entryPoint. Newly minted this run; verified to reproduce from fingerprintBasis and not to collide with any of the 19 pre-existing ledger fingerprints. Minted on the NEW function name `annihilate`, which is correct and is not fingerprint drift.

routing.binding: SPEC-CONFORMANCE ONLY - NEVER THE QA BUNDLE, AT ANY BAND. Law 2 is a routing law before it is a severity law (CRITICAL RULE 6), so the routing does not move with the band. Must NOT be collapsed into Q-05: collapsing them would hide the F-01 tripwire inside a process finding.

storyTag: none (untagged commit c91bc1a, subject 'more precise mint requirement')
specText: story-001, Required deltas #5 (lines 122-126): 'Everything else - the check order, the burn-before-interactions ordering, the balance snapshots, the forceApprove/reset pair, the StableNotDeposited and PhUSDNotReceived assertions, the split _phUSD.mint(recipient, amount) + safeTransfer(recipient, mintedForStable) delivery - stays exactly as it is. This story is a signature and authorisation change, not a rewrite of the settlement logic.'
actualBehavior: c91bc1a - untagged, landed after both story commits - adds a pre-loop quote at :231-232 (`expectedForStable = minter.calculateMintAmount(...)`; `if (expectedForStable == 0) revert PhUSDNotReceived();`) and replaces the post-hoc `if (mintedForStable == 0) revert PhUSDNotReceived();` with `if (mintedForStable != expectedForStable) revert PhUSDAmountMismatch(expectedForStable, mintedForStable);` at :248. A new error is declared and PhUSDNotReceived is REPURPOSED to mean 'the quote itself was zero', now raised BEFORE the burn instead of after it. 51 lines of new tests accompany it.
deviation: Neither story sanctions a change to the phUSD settlement post-condition. Story-001 names the PhUSDNotReceived assertion in an explicit do-not-touch list and says the story is 'not a rewrite of the settlement logic'; story-002 is confined to toStableAmount. This is un-storied work riding on a two-story fix-wave, and the fix-wave's traceability (H-01 <- story-001, M-01 <- story-002) does not extend to it.

classification.assetImpact: NONE. The new post-condition is strictly stricter than the one it replaces: every state the old check accepted and the new one rejects is a state in which the caller received less than, or differently from, the minter's own quote. Substantively the change implements run-01 F-01's own recommended mitigation TEXT almost verbatim and narrows ledger L-01's donation-attribution gap.

justification: Low, routed to spec-conformance. Law 2 is a routing law before it is a severity law, and that routing is not negotiable at any band. On the band: the code is safe, tested, strictly stricter than what it replaced, and is substantially the audit's own recommendation, so there is no security escalation and Medium is not in play. It is not QA either, for a checkable reason: an unreviewed, untagged behavioural change to annihilate's settlement post-condition landed in the SAME delta as the fixes for the project's only open High and its open Medium, in the one function every open finding passes through, story-001 had explicitly placed that assertion out of bounds, AND story-001's acceptance checklist still carries a ticked box asserting it was preserved. Because nothing in the story tree records the decision, there are no acceptance criteria against which a future regression of this post-condition could be graded - the gap is durable and it is exactly what a story-faithfulness pass exists to make visible. Law 2 is GRADED here, not deferred: the story tree resolved this run and stories 001 and 002 were read in full. This is not a 'story unavailable' non-answer.
interactionWithQ05: The same untagged commit that over-claims its coverage in Q-05's comment is the commit no story authorises here. Both point at the same missing review, but they are DELIBERATELY NOT COLLAPSED: Q-05 carries the F-01 false-closure tripwire and belongs in the QA bundle; F-04 is a Law-2 provenance deviation and belongs in spec-conformance only.
recommendation: LEAD WITH THIS: NO CODE CHANGE IS REQUIRED. The code is safe and is substantially the audit's own recommended mitigation; this finding is not criticism of the fix. Write the story - or amend story-002 / add story-003 - recording this decision, its acceptance criteria and its failure-mode analysis, so the exact-equality post-condition has a documented intent to be graded against in future regressions. Correct story-001's acceptance checklist at line 198, which now certifies a preservation that no longer holds. When the new story is written, address Q-05 in it: the comment at :232-233 claims coverage the check does not provide, and the story is the right place to decide whether the intent is the narrow check that exists or the slippage guard the comment describes.

supersedes.handling: CONSOLIDATED INTO THIS RECORD - not deleted content. The upstream draft's unique analysis is folded in below (failureBehaviourAnalysis, errorSemanticsChange) with two CORRECTIONS recorded in reObservationsCorrected. Exactly one F-04 record exists so a reader cannot end up with two divergent accounts of the same fingerprint.

additionalContext.failureBehaviourAnalysis: The audit brief hypothesised that a partially-binding daily cap could make the minter's actual mint differ from its own quote, so that a previously-succeeding annihilation now reverts. That hypothesis is NEGATIVE for this minter: PhusdStableMinter.mint:221 enforces the cap as `require(config.mintedToday + phUSDAmount <= config.maxMintPerDay, "Daily mint limit exceeded")` - all-or-nothing, never a partial mint - and it calls the same calculateMintAmount on the same config in the same transaction. The only reachable divergence is extra phUSD arriving on Antimatter between the phUSDBefore snapshot (:135) and the delta read (:147), i.e. a callback from a hookful stablecoin during safeTransferFrom or from the yield strategy during minter.mint. That case previously over-credited the caller-chosen recipient (open ledger L-01) and now reverts. No legitimate flow that succeeded before c91bc1a fails after it.
additionalContext.errorSemanticsChange: PhUSDNotReceived is retained by name but now means 'the minter's quote was zero' and fires pre-burn; the case it used to signal ('the minter delivered nothing') now surfaces as PhUSDAmountMismatch(expected, 0). Any off-chain monitor keying on the old selector's meaning is silently re-pointed. Neither story mentions the rename or the semantic shift.

reObservationsCorrected.note: The upstream draft's reObservations are RETAINED BUT CORRECTED. Both of its closure-adjacent statements are dangerous as written and are overridden by the sanitizer's binding rulings.

This is WATCH-02-02, the highest-probability false closure in the whole delta. See Q-05.falseClosureBlock for the attestation required before F-01 (3aac91383dcb6060) may ever be marked fixed.

L-01.correction: L-01 IS NOT CLOSED.
